questionText:
Consider a computer system with a byte-addressable primary memory of size $2^{32}$ bytes. Assume the computer system has a direct-mapped cache of size 32 KB ($1 \text{ KB} = 2^{10}$ bytes), and each cache block is of size 64 bytes.

The size of the tag field is _________ bits.
explanation:
Step 1: Determine total physical address bits
Primary memory size = $2^{32}$ bytes.
Since memory is byte-addressable, Physical Address = 32 bits.

Step 2: Calculate Block Offset bits
Cache block size = $64\text{ bytes} = 2^6\text{ bytes}$.
Block offset bits = $\log_2(64) = 6\text{ bits}$.

Step 3: Calculate Index bits
Cache size = $32\text{ KB} = 32 \times 2^{10}\text{ bytes} = 2^{15}\text{ bytes}$.
Number of cache lines = $\frac{\text{Cache Size}}{\text{Block Size}} = \frac{2^{15}}{2^6} = 2^9$.
Index bits = $\log_2(2^9) = 9\text{ bits}$.

Step 4: Calculate Tag bits
Physical Address = Tag bits + Index bits + Block offset bits
$32 = \text{Tag bits} + 9 + 6$
$\text{Tag bits} = 32 - 15 = 17\text{ bits}$.
